content.en: Mangroves are salt-tolerant wetland forest communities inhabiting intertidal coastal zones of tropics and subtropics, exhibiting remarkable physiological adaptations to hypersaline and anaerobic soils.
content.hi: Mangroves are salt-tolerant wetland forest communities inhabiting intertidal coastal zones of tropics and subtropics, exhibiting remarkable physiological adaptations to hypersaline and anaerobic soils.

content.en:
• Specialized Adaptations: Pneumatophores (blind vertical breathing roots with lenticels for gas exchange), Stilt roots (mechanical anchoring against tidal waves), Vivipary (seeds germinate while still attached to parent tree), Salt-secreting glands on leaves.
• World distribution: 40% in Asia. Sunderbans is the largest mangrove delta globally.
• Ecological roles: Tsunami bio-shield, blue carbon sequestration, nursery for estuarine fishes, and sediment trapping.

question.en: Which physiological adaptation enables mangrove plants to reproduce successfully in saline, waterlogged soils?
question.hi: Which physiological adaptation enables mangrove plants to reproduce successfully in saline, waterlogged soils?

explanation.en: Vivipary (where seeds germinate and develop into seedlings while still attached to the parent tree before dropping into water/soil) prevents seeds from being asphyxiated in anaerobic saline mud.
